sentences.text: Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 28-10-2022 at about 7.20 p.m., the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road near Neralekere Bus Stand, Bangarpet-KGF road, Bangarpet Taluk, KGF.
At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EL-8100 came in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Bangarpet, wherein he took first aid treatment and later he was shifted to S.N.R. Hospital, Kolar and Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as mason and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Bangarpet Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.

The respondent No.1 is the owner,
respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted that, the respondent No.1 company is the owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EL-8100, the said vehicle is insured with the respondent No.2, the policy was valid as on the date of accident and the rider Pravin L. Vaishnav was possessing a valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident.
It has denied the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

Likewise, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of motorcycle bearing No. KA-41- EL-8100 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 28-10-2022 at about 7:20 p.m.,
due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-41-EL-8100 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.
Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Ramesh as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its authorized representative as R.W.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed its side.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 28-10-2022 at about 7.20 p.m., when he was walking on the left side of the road near Neralekere Bus Stand, Bangarpet- KGF road, Bangarpet Taluk, KGF, the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EL-8100 came in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to him from behind and caused grievous injuries to him.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as mason and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.

But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled Srinivas vs Metals And Steels Pvt Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44041159/

sentences.text: 11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is true copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.8 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.9 is discharge summary, Ex.P.10 are medical bills (total 15), Ex.P.11 are x-rays (total 5), Ex.P.12 and 13 are photographs (total 2), Ex.P.14 is CD, Ex.P.15 is case-sheet, Ex.P.16 is out patient book and Ex.P.17 is X-ray.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, on 28-10- 2022 at about 7.20 p.m., when the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road near Neralekere Bus Stand, Bangarpet-KGF road, Bangarpet Taluk, KGF, the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EL-8100 came in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to him from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report, which is marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EL-8100 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EL-8100 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further though the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the averments made in the petition, with respect to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EL-8100 and taken specific contention that, the said accident is caused due to careless and self negligence on the part of the petitioner himself, who was walking on the road without observing traffic rules and regulations, they have not adduced any evidence or produced any document to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statement of the representative of respondent No.1, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 & 2 to show that, the said accident is caused due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and not due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle.

Further,
there is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on extreme left side of 30 feet wide Bangarpet-KGF road, near Neralekere Bus Stand,
Bangarpet Taluk, KGF, due to dashing of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EL-8100 to the Srinivas vs Metals And Steels Pvt Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44041159/
4 pedestrian/petitioner from behind.

sentences.text: Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EL-8100.

Admittedly,
the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA- 41-EL-8100.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary,
Ex.P.11 x-rays (total 5), Ex.P.15 case-sheet, Ex.P.16 out-patient book and Ex.P.17 x-ray
, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered fracture left distal 1/3rd shaft of tibia and fibula.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has treated the petitioner and examined him for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, he has treated the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident taken place on 28-10-2022 and the petitioner had suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
18.

No. KA-41-EL- 8100.

19. Issue No.2:

sentences.text: While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EL-8100 and he has sustained fracture of left distal 1/3rd shaft of tibia and fibula and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8, the year of birth of the petitioner is 1963.
The accident has taken place on 28-10- 2022 at about 7:20 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 59 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture left distal 1/3rd shaft of tibia and fibula.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 28%
physical disability of left lower limb and 14% physical disability for the whole body of the petitioner.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.11 x-rays (total 5), Ex.P.15 case sheet, Ex.P.16 out patient book and Ex.P.17 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered fracture left distal 1/3rd shaft of tibia and fibula.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.
Further he has denied that, there are no restrictions of movements to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 28-10-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 30-09-2023, which is after lapse of eleven months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the fracture is united.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 7% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence, in the instant case the disability of Srinivas vs Metals And Steels Pvt Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44041159/
6 7% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

sentences.text: a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as mason and was earning income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do mason work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was doing mason work.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court,
except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 59 years is 9.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 7/100 X 9 = Rs.1,17,180/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 15 medical bills, as per Ex.P.10.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.8,792/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,792/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
suffered fracture left distal 1/3rd shaft of tibia and fibula.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 18 days from 29-10-2022 to 15- 11-2022, in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 18 days from 29-10-2022 to 15-11-2022, in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.1000 x 18 = Rs.18,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 18 days from 29-10-2022 to 15-11-2022, in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.800 x 18 = Rs.14,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.

sentences.text: The petitioner is the resident of Soregowdanakote, Bangarpet, Kolar, the accident has taken place near Neralekere Bus Stand, Bangarpet-KGF road, Bangarpet Taluk, KGF and the petitioner has taken treatment at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between both the places, compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 18 days as inpatient at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 2 =
Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 59 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture left distal 1/3rd shaft of tibia and fibula.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 7% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his cross-examination that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and the cost of surgery would be Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/-.
But, admittedly he has not issued estimation of cost for the alleged surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 1,17,180-00 2.
Medical expenses 8,792-00 3. Pain and sufferings 20,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 18,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 14,400-00 6. Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 10,000-00 Total Rs. 2,43,372-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,43,372/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-) from the date of Srinivas vs Metals And Steels Pvt Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44041159/
8 petition till its realization.
21. Liability:

entities.text: Srinivas vs Metals And Steels Pvt Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EL-8100 the said accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,43,372/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,43,372/- (Rupees two lakh forty-three thousand three hundred and seventy two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Bangarpet Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments: The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 28-10-2022 at about 7:20 p.m.,
due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-41-EL-8100 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.

21. Liability:
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,43,372/- (Rupees two lakh forty-three thousand three hundred and seventy two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of petitioner as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
